messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty page fired for service=canary-release-v2, alert=5xx-rate-up, priority=high. Details: route=embed-service, cluster=us-west-2, rollout=canary-42

pagerduty-bot: Page assigned to sre-tilly (pager duty incident #INC-2028). Auto-escalation scheduled in 8m if unack'd.

sre-tilly: acked. pulling graphs now. can someone drop the canary traffic policy?

eng-runtime-maya: on it. confirming the canary only has ~8% traffic, but 5xx spike at p95 token path.

eng-platform-jon: seeing elevated host OOM counts on canary nodes in us-west-2-gpupool-a, kernel logs show `OOM killer invoked for process python` around the same window.

support-luis: any customer-facing impact yet? receiving a ticket from cust: terra-data that they saw 503s on embeddings this morning.

product-ops-ana: ETA on mitigation? If customers are hit we should pause rollout and divert to previous variant.

eng-runtime-maya: recommended immediate mitigation: 1) pause canary rollout 2) divert 100% of traffic for embed route to stable model v1.9 3) drain canary nodes. can do quick switch via traffic-split flag.

sre-tilly: +1 to pause and divert. posting the command I'll run:

```
# pause rollout and flip traffic
redwoodctl rollout pause canary-release-v2 --id canary-42
redwoodctl traffic update --route embed-service --weights v1.9=100,v2=0
```

eng-platform-jon: logs attached from affected instance (truncated):
```
[2026-03-15T02:11:04Z] python[2456]: Alloc failed: requested 6.0G, available 3.2G
[2026-03-15T02:11:04Z] kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 2456 (python) score 120
[2026-03-15T02:11:05Z] envoy: 5xx from upstream embed-worker/10.12.3.7: failed to accept request
```

sre-tilly: running the pause now, then traffic flip. will update when done.

sre-tilly: done. rollout paused and route switched to v1.9. Canary nodes are marked drain. Observed error rate for embed-service dropped from 6.2% -> 0.4% in the last 2m.

support-luis: sent note to terra-data: "we detected elevated error rates on today's canary, we've rolled back their traffic to the stable model and are investigating; no action required on your side."

cust-success-kate: pinging top 3 impacted accounts to confirm service stability. will log any follow-ups.

eng-runtime-maya: quick triage summary: v2 introduced a change to KV cache prefetch that increases memory pressure under certain sequence-length distributions. reproducing locally with long prompts. Next steps: 1) reproduce on staging with stress harness 2) add guardrail to abort if memory headroom < 10% 3) patch runtime to avoid prefetch race.

product-ops-ana: please capture the canary's config + model checksum and attach to the incident ticket. we'll need to block this variant from future canaries until fix.

eng-runtime-maya: posted artifact: model_sha256=ab12f9c... and config snippet in the incident ticket.

pagerduty-bot: Incident INC-2028 updated: status=mitigated, assigned_to=sre-tilly, severity=high -> triage.

sre-tilly: moving to postmortem channel once we have root cause. brief impact: ~12 customers saw transient 5xx (mostly retries succeeded), two enterprise customers reported brief failures in embedding ingestion jobs; no data loss.

eng-platform-jon: we'll add node-level OOM alerting thresholds to catch this earlier (p95 mem free < 1GB). filing infra ticket.

support-luis: adding tags to support tickets for faster routing: `incident:5187654321`

cust-success-kate: logged outreach: terra-data (ack'ed), alpha-analytics (monitoring), fintech-hub (no impact).

product-ops-ana: action items: 1) eng-runtime to hotfix prefetch guard 2) eng-platform to add mem alerts + safer autoscale 3) rollout policy change: require extra safety net for memory-allocating model variants 4) update runbook to include rapid traffic-diversion commands.

eng-runtime-maya: will push a staged fix and run a controlled canary later today with stricter memory caps.

sre-tilly: closing the immediate page — marking incident as mitigated. follow-up postmortem to be posted to #postmortems/production with timeline and impact metrics. thanks all. :thumbsup:
